newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Premier resigns in S.Africa's Zulu province.
newsitem.headline: Premier resigns in S.Africa's Zulu province.

text.p: Frank Mdlalose, the chairman of South Africa's Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party and premier of KwaZulu-Natal province, has resigned from both positions, party leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi said on Saturday.

Mdlalose has been closely involved with African National Congress chairman Jacob Zuma in trying to quell fighting between supporters of their rival parties which has killed some 14,000 people in the province over the past decade.
Zuma said the fragile peace process would not be affected.
"Although his resignation came as a surprise it is not going to affect the peace process because the process is bigger than individual leaders," Zuma told Reuters.
Buthelezi told a party congress that Mdlalose was resigning for personal and health reasons. Officials said he would probably step down at the end of February.
The announcement came barely a month after Buthelezi threatened to cut out the dead wood in the party and restructure the Zulu-based party ahead of the 1999 national elections.

Officials said he would be replaced temporarily as chairman and possibly as premier by Ben Ngubane, who was taken from a position in President Nelson Mandela's national unity government last year to join the Inkatha-dominated provincial government.
